source.title: Signal-to-Noise Ratio and Sample Size Govern Representational Alignment in Neural Networks

record.tranche_reason: Measures alignment between independently trained networks and tests how it changes with training-data noise and sample size, using CCE rather than the original studies' measures.
record.gate_note: The study reports alignment results for linear networks, ReLU networks, and classification networks under varied data conditions. Generalization-error results alone are not alignment results. The linear-versus-ReLU comparison is included under fits_no_version because it compares architectures but does not test convergence with scale or capability.
record.test_reason: It measures alignment (CCE) between independently trained networks and shows alignment is incomplete and can vanish. That bears only on V7's 'alignment stays far from complete' part. It does not vary model scale or measurement choices, so V1 and V6 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that CCE alignment rises monotonically with SNR and varies non-monotonically with sample size, with a minimum near the interpolation threshold, in every network they tried. They also conclude that alignment and representational informativeness are decoupled from generalization, so task performance is an insufficient proxy for representation quality.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Conditional Copula Entropy, a rank-based measure of neighborhood predictability, rather than the measures used in the cited alignment literature; tests controlled data-quality and sample-size changes rather than model scaling or cross-modal convergence.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment changes with SNR or label-noise level and training sample size; the study reports minima near interpolation thresholds.

fits_no_version.finding: Alignment rises monotonically with SNR, and falls with label noise. It varies non-monotonically with sample size, with a minimum at the interpolation threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alignment between independently trained networks is governed by training-data quality and quantity, with a minimum at the interpolation threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: Networks with equal generalization error show different alignment. Better-generalizing networks can be less aligned. ReLU representations are more informative than linear ones despite worse generalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representational alignment and informativeness are decoupled from task performance.

record.problems: Most alignment values are reported in figures without numerical values in the text. Several results are averages over experiments, but uncertainty magnitudes are not stated. The empirical tests use limited, specific architectures and single-modality tasks; the theoretical linear result assumes a shared singular-vector basis and low-rank structure.
record.rows_left_out: Generalization-error curves were omitted because they do not measure alignment. No other alignment results were omitted.

untested.parts: Model size and capability scaling across architectures, objectives and data. Sample size is varied instead, and model width is fixed.
All parts; the study is single-modality.
Shared features or subspaces across seeds. Networks differ in training data, and the CIFAR networks share initialization.
All parts; no mapping or stitching.
Dependence on the similarity measure, its settings (e.g. neighbour count), evaluation inputs or out-of-distribution data. Only CCE is used.
Plateau with scale, and shared data/objective versus a common-reality explanation.

missing.what: Closed-form prediction ρ* = SNR/(SNR + 1/(α−1)) for α>1 (and an analogous form for α<1), which bounds alignment below 1 at finite SNR
Comparison of generalization error (panels a) with CCE (panels b) showing alignment decoupled from performance

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 links were wrong. The study varies training data, not measurement choices, so the V6 label is removed. The V7 verdict covers only the incompleteness of alignment; the study tests neither the plateau nor the cause of alignment. All models are small and of fixed width, and values are read from figures only.

versions.untested_parts: The study varies training sample size, not model size or capability, and does not compare independently trained models across the architectures, objectives, and datasets specified in this version.
No vision-language pair or paired images and captions; the study describes its experiments as single-modality.
The study measures rank-based distance alignment, not whether particular features or shared subspaces recur across seeds.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test.
No test of recurring interpretable features or circuits.
Tests variation with training SNR or label noise and sample size using CCE. Does not compare similarity measures, vary metric settings such as neighbour count, or test out-of-distribution inputs.

Reports conditional and sometimes near-zero alignment, but does not test whether alignment plateaus at large model scale or compare shared-data/objective explanations against a common-model-of-reality explanation.

rows.subject: two-layer linear network
rows.operation_detail: Measured CCE between hidden representations of identical networks trained on independent datasets.

conditions.value: varied; individual plotted values not stated in text

rows.uncertainty: Dots with bars; bar magnitudes not stated. Numerical results averaged over 50 independent experiments.
rows.note: Text reports that CCE increases with SNR and varies non-monotonically with α, increasing away from the interpolation threshold.
rows.check: Removed V6: SNR and sample size are training-data properties, not similarity-measure settings or evaluation inputs. For V7, the theory gives ρ*<1 at any finite SNR, so alignment is incomplete and varies with conditions.

source_check.correct: state=observed for the tested incompleteness component of V7: the theoretical correlation is below one at finite SNR and finite sample ratio, and alignment vanishes at interpolation.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4.1, Theorem 1, Equations 12 and 15, Figure 1(b), pp. 5–6.
source_check.problem: The state describes incomplete alignment as partial evidence, although incomplete alignment is itself the tested V7 effect.

rows.subject: two-layer linear network
rows.operation_detail: Measured CCE at the interpolation threshold between hidden representations of identical networks trained on independent datasets.

conditions.value: finite SNR > 0; text says result is regardless of SNR

rows.value: figure only; text reports CCE(A → B) ≈ 0
rows.uncertainty: Dots with bars; bar magnitudes not stated. Numerical results averaged over 50 independent experiments.
rows.note: The authors interpret this as essentially no alignment between the representations at the interpolation threshold.
rows.check: Removed V6. Near-zero CCE at α=1 means alignment essentially vanishes, which is what V7 describes. The state 'absent' described alignment itself, not the V7 effect.

rows.subject: two-layer network with ReLU activation
rows.operation_detail: Measured CCE between hidden representations of networks trained on independent datasets.

conditions.value: varied; individual plotted values not stated in text
γ = n/p varied, where p = d × k

rows.uncertainty: Numerical results averaged over 50 independent experiments; uncertainty magnitudes not stated.
rows.note: Text reports a non-monotonic sample-size pattern with a sharp minimum near γ ≈ 1, and higher alignment at larger SNR in both regimes.
rows.check: Removed V6. Alignment is SNR-dependent with a sharp minimum near γ≈1; it is incomplete but not a full collapse.

source_check.correct: state=observed for the tested V7 component: alignment has a sharp minimum near γ≈1 and is lower at smaller SNR in both sample-size regimes.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4.2, Figure 2 caption and accompanying discussion, p. 7.
source_check.problem: Reduced, condition-dependent alignment is the observed V7 effect; partial incorrectly describes the degree of alignment instead.

rows.subject: two-layer network with ReLU activation
rows.operation_detail: Measured CCE near the interpolation threshold between hidden representations.
rows.value: figure only; text says CCE converges to an SNR-dependent value and does not approach zero
rows.uncertainty: Numerical results averaged over 50 independent experiments; uncertainty magnitudes not stated.
rows.note: Unlike the linear case, the threshold does not eliminate alignment; the value remains dependent on SNR.
rows.check: Removed V6. Reduced but nonzero alignment at the threshold shows incomplete convergence.

rows.subject: standard convolutional neural network (CNN)
rows.size_stated: 40 feature maps in the last convolutional layer
rows.operation_detail: Measured CCE between penultimate representations of identical networks trained on non-overlapping subsets.

conditions.value: varied; individual plotted rates not stated in text

rows.note: Text reports that lower label noise gives better alignment than higher label noise in both sample-size regimes, and that alignment varies non-monotonically with a minimum near the interpolation threshold.
rows.check: Removed V6. Both networks start from the same initialization, so only the training data differ. No numbers are given.

source_check.correct: state=observed for the tested V7 component: alignment decreases with label noise and has a minimum near the interpolation threshold.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4.3, Figure 4 caption and accompanying discussion, pp. 8–9.
source_check.problem: The reported reductions establish the tested V7 effect; partial describes alignment rather than the linked claim.

rows.subject: fully connected neural network
rows.size_stated: single hidden layer; number of hidden units not stated
rows.operation_detail: Measured CCE between penultimate representations of identical networks trained on independent datasets.

conditions.value: varied; individual plotted rates not stated in text
ratio to number of network parameters; plotted values not stated in text

rows.locator: Figure 5(b), Appendix F.2; qualitative summary in Section 4.3
rows.note: The main text says the MNIST results are qualitatively similar to the CIFAR-10 results; the appendix figure is not described in further detail.

rows.subject: linear network and ReLU network
rows.operation_detail: Measured directional CCE between hidden representations of a linear network and a ReLU network.
rows.uncertainty: Numerical results averaged over 20 independent experiments; uncertainty magnitudes not stated.
rows.note: The text says the ReLU representation is more informative than the linear representation overall, but does not specify the directional CCE values in the figure.
rows.check: Cross-architecture alignment at fixed size with no scale variation. Directional values appear only in the figure.

rows.subject: linear network and ReLU network
rows.operation_detail: Measured directional CCE between hidden representations of a ReLU network and a linear network.
rows.uncertainty: Numerical results averaged over 20 independent experiments; uncertainty magnitudes not stated.
rows.note: The text reports that at n/d × k = 0.05 the CCE collapses to zero, and that the ReLU network has a local minimum at its interpolation threshold, n/d × k = 1. It does not give the directional values in the figure.
rows.check: Same as R7. The collapse to zero at n/(d×k)=0.05 is reported for the CCE between the two networks, not specifically for one direction.

relationships.condition: Small linear, ReLU, CNN and FCNN networks of identical architecture trained on independent samples of the same task
relationships.reason: Alignment is incomplete: ρ*<1 at finite SNR (R1). It vanishes at the linear interpolation threshold (R2) and is reduced at the ReLU threshold (R4). It falls with noise (R3, R5).
relationships.display_finding: Alignment remained below 1 at finite signal-to-noise ratios, vanished at the linear interpolation threshold, weakened at the ReLU threshold and declined with noise.

relation.reason: Its own results measure alignment and identify conditions where it decreases or vanishes.

tranche.reason: Introduces CCE and uses analytical and numerical experiments to test representational alignment under changes in training noise and sample size.

source_check.notes: V7 support concerns incomplete alignment, not its proposed causal explanation; CCE reductions alone do not quantify distance from complete alignment. The linear theory assumes a shared covariance eigenbasis and low-rank first-layer weights.

reader_labels.condition: Training-data SNR or label noise and sample size in the tested single-modality settings
reader_labels.reason: Alignment changes with SNR or label noise and sample size, but the study uses CCE alone and does not vary metric settings or test out-of-distribution inputs (R1-R6).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Independent training runs on the same task or data-generating setup
reader_labels.reason: The reported alignment is conditional rather than uniform: it varies with sample size and data noise, and is essentially absent for linear networks at α = 1 (R1-R6).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Experiments sharing a task or data-generating setup
reader_labels.reason: These results do not establish whether shared data or objectives, rather than a common model of reality, explain the alignment; the study does not compare those explanations (R1-R6).
